content: The clinical significance of this finding is supported by a more substantial reduction in pain intensity over a 24-hour period in patients treated with Caldolor, even though morphine was available on an as-needed basis. In a study involving patients who underwent elective abdominal or orthopedic surgery, a total of 406 patients (87 men and 319 women) were randomized to receive either Caldolor 400 mg, Caldolor 800 mg, or a placebo administered every 6 hours, starting intra-operatively. Morphine was also provided on an as-needed basis. This study did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in outcomes between patients receiving Caldolor (800 mg or 400 mg) and those receiving a placebo, although there were trends favoring the active treatments. Antipyretic (Fever): The effect of Caldolor on fever was evaluated in two randomized, double-blind studies. 1. In a multi-center study, 120 hospitalized patients (88 men and 32 women) with temperatures of 101°F or greater were randomized to receive Caldolor 400 mg, 200 mg, 100 mg, or a placebo, administered every 4 hours for 24 hours. Each of the three Caldolor doses (100 mg, 200 mg, and 400 mg) resulted in a statistically greater percentage of patients achieving a reduced temperature (<101°F) after 4 hours compared to the placebo group. The percentages were 65%, 73%, 77%, and 32%, respectively, demonstrating a dose-response relationship. 2. In a single-center study, 60 hospitalized patients (48 men and 12 women) with uncomplicated fever were randomized to receive either Caldolor 400 mg or a placebo, administered every 6 hours for 72 hours. The study demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in fever over time in patients treated with Caldolor compared to the placebo group. How Supplied: Caldolor is available in the following strength: 800 mg/8 mL (100 mg/mL) Packaged in a carton of 25 vials, NDC 66220-287-08 Storage: Store at controlled room temperature, between 20°C to 25°C (68°F to 77°F). Patient Counseling Information: There is limited information available regarding patient counseling for ibuprofen (injection) in the drug label. Precautions with Alcohol: The interaction between alcohol and ibuprofen (injection) has not been established. Patients should consult their doctor regarding the potential effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication.
